## TL;DR

Implemented allowlist groups (#1132): a project opts in with
`budget.allowlistGroup = "<name>"`, the group's CLIs/models/pause state live in
`~/.config/repoos/allowlist-groups/<name>.toml` (versioned, last-writer-wins,
never committed, no secrets), and projects without a group keep the exact
project-only behaviour. Pause/resume from Budget Controls or
`repoos allowlist pause|resume` updates the group, reaches local members through
the shared file, and reaches same-group tailnet members over authenticated SSH
after listing them in a confirmation dialog. Budget Controls shows the group,
per-entry provenance, drift and Re-sync. Tests cover the merge table, store,
config parsing, member filtering, remote outcome classification, group isolation
and the UI flow.

## Work and rationale

**Where group state lives.** The group cannot live in any repo's committed
`repoos.toml`: that is what forced the 15 Nov hand-edits, and remote updates must
never edit another repo's committed files. It is machine-local coordination
state, so each group is one small TOML file under
`~/.config/repoos/allowlist-groups/` (overridable with
`REPOOS_ALLOWLIST_GROUPS_DIR`, mirroring `tunnel-apps.toml`'s XDG location).
`version` is bumped on every write and `updatedAt` is the ISO write time; a
receiver accepts only a newer `updatedAt`, with `version` as a tie-breaker. The
parser keeps only the five allowlist fields, so a credential cannot be smuggled
in, and names are validated as filenames to stop path traversal.

**Merge semantics.** `mergeAllowlistRows(groupRows, projectRows)` treats the
group as the base and the project's rows as overrides: models union (so a project
can add a model without losing the group's), a pause on either side remains a
pause (a local row cannot silently un-pause what the group paused), and
per-model pauses merge by model with the project winning for that model.
Project-only agents append. Empty group rows return the project rows unchanged,
so the no-group path is byte-for-byte the old behaviour; the test table covers
each case. `allowlistSources` and `allowlistDrift` share the same merge so the UI
cannot disagree with enforcement. Re-sync drops only project rows for CLIs the
group defines, keeping project-only additions.

**Config loading.** `loadConfig` reads the project rows through the existing
runtime-pause hydration, then reads and merges the group. A missing group file is
normal (the project works alone until the group is created); a corrupt one
warns and keeps the project rows rather than silently un-pausing everything.
`budget.allowlistGroup` got a schema entry, a supported-keys entry, user-docs and
a Budget Controls control (the schema entry is search metadata, skipped by the
generic Settings form so an unrelated save never rewrites it). The config PATCH
route validates the name, joins/leaves the group, and removes the key when
cleared instead of leaving `= ""`.

**Propagation.** Pause/resume writes the local group file and reloads the live
config. Members on the same machine need no per-repo write: they share the file,
and `ConfigWatcher` now includes the group file in its change signature, so a
running server adopts the pause within one poll interval. Remote members are
discovered with the same trusted path as #1127: registry entries publish
`allowlistGroup`, `repoos servers --json` carries it, and only rows declaring the
same group name are members; unreachable rows are excluded because their group is
unknown. Each remote member gets
`cd <member root> && repoos allowlist group apply --payload-base64 … --check-logins`
over the SSH credentials discovery already uses. The HTTP apply route is behind
the normal auth middleware, and both receivers verify the local checkout declares
the group and refuse older state. The API never accepts a caller-supplied host
list, so it cannot become an arbitrary remote-exec endpoint. Results are
`applied` / `unreachable` / `refused` per member; each receiver also reports
allowed CLIs it is not logged in to, never syncing logins.

**UI.** Budget Controls gained a group card (name, updated time, Change/Join),
`group`/`project` badges per row, a drift banner with Re-sync, a per-member
results list, and a pause dialog that lists the projects and hosts before the
change goes out and offers a "send to other machines" checklist. When a project
is grouped, add/remove/pause/resume mutate the group (the group owns the shared
list) and a local-only CLI still falls back to the project's own rows; the CLI
does the same check. The member list is fetched when the dialog opens, not on
every page load, to keep the tab fast.

## Approaches tried

- Considered a new HTTP write endpoint for peers. Rejected: cross-server session
  cookies do not exist, and inventing a shared token would create a new secret to
  store. SSH is already the trust path discovery uses; the HTTP route stays for
  the local UI and tests, behind session auth.
- Considered merging per field by replacing the project row wholesale. Union for
  models and pause-wins is less surprising and preserves the "group pause reaches
  everyone" guarantee; wholesale replacement let a stale local row un-pause the
  group.
- Considered making the UI recompute drift/merge in the browser. The server
  already merges for enforcement; sharing that function keeps the badge, drift
  and what actually runs from drifting apart.
- Considered a per-repo watcher for group changes. Extending the existing config
  signature (repoos.toml + group file) was a smaller change and reuses the reload
  path already proven for hand edits.

## Challenges and blockers

- Circular imports: the group module needs a TOML reader, and config.ts needs the
  merge. Rather than making `config.ts` import itself, the group module has a
  small purpose-built reader for the one shape it writes; malformed structure is
  `invalid`, not an empty group.
- Remote members were briefly double-counted because discovery repeats this
  machine's registry rows. The state builder now takes local membership from the
  registry and only adds remote rows from discovery.
- Real multi-host propagation needs a live tailnet with logged-in machines. Tests
  cover discovery filtering and the SSH request/response contract with a fake
  transport; I did not observe applied state on bee or thinkpad, so the task
  should note a human tailnet verification is still desirable. No device or
  external-account results are claimed.

## Key learnings

- Group state is machine state, not project source: keeping it out of git removes
  the whole class of "now edit and commit four repos" work and makes the
  last-writer-wins rule natural.
- A merge rule that lets a local row un-pause a group would silently break the
  core promise. Pause-wins is the safe default, and the UI's drift warning makes
  intentional local overrides visible instead of hidden.
- Reusing the existing discovery and config-watch seams kept the feature small:
  no new network daemon, no new credential, no second reload mechanism.
